title: Declarative private VPC networking profiles and upgrade acceptance criteria
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Provide a concise, testable PRD that defines declarative networking profiles for Private/VPC deployments and explicit acceptance criteria for upgrades when clusters operate under restricted egress (air-gapped or proxy-only). This ticket captures requirements for: 1) profile definitions and validation, 2) operator behavior during control-plane and data-plane upgrades, 3) allowed telemetry and audit hooks in zero-egress environments, and 4) deterministic failover/fallback modes for image/artifact procurement. The intent is to unblock ENG for implementation and QA for integration tests and acceptance automation.
summary_of_requirements: Declarative networking profiles: customers choose from named profiles (zero-egress, proxy-egress, staged-mirror, outbound-allowed) with documented contract semantics.
Validation: control-plane validates supplied profile at bootstrap and rejects incompatible combinations (eg. zero-egress + remote-provisioning).
Upgrade contracts: operator must support offline image validation, staged image activation, and rollback windows with deterministic operator state transitions documented.
Telemetry contract: minimal, customer-consented telemetry allowed in airgapped modes via signed bundles or local push to preconfigured collector endpoints.
Per-namespace egress intent: support policy that allows per-tenant exceptions declared with explicit justification and audit trail.
Operator fallback modes: when primary artifact mirror unreachable, operator engages configured fallback (local cache, scheduled retry, operator-initiated degraded-mode) with clear SLA consequences.
Acceptance tests: automated harness that can simulate partitioned network, proxy auth failures, and offline-only bootstrap in CI sandbox.
Documentation & runbook: end-to-end upgrade playbook for zero-egress customers and checklist for SRE/Support handoffs.
Backward compatibility: profile API must be additive; older control planes must still honor minimal subset and surface clear migration warnings.
Security: KMS-backed manifest verification for offline images and signed operator binaries required for zero-egress validation.
Observability: in no-egress mode, operator must emit local audit logs and provide a secure export mechanism customers can pull on-demand.
Rollout policy: canary policy supports fully-airgapped canary (staged mirror) and must provide deterministic rollback triggers tied to health and integrity checks.
acceptance_criteria: Profile semantics documented in PRD: each profile has a 1-paragraph description, allowed configuration keys, and failure modes.
Bootstrap validation: creating a cluster with a declared profile either succeeds or returns an explicit, machine-readable rejection reason and remediation steps.
Offline upgrade flow: operator can perform image activation without external egress using pre-staged artifacts and validation finishes within documented time bounds.
Canary in airgap: a simulated canary run using staged-mirror profile completes a critical request path test and signals success/failure to the console.
Telemetry gating: console shows exact telemetry items permitted for airgapped deployments and the customer consent token is honored end-to-end.
Auditable exceptions: any per-namespace egress exceptions are recorded with rationale, approver, and timestamp; audit export can be pulled and parsed by compliance teams.

Fallback behavior: when primary mirror is unavailable, operator enters fallback mode and surfaces clear actionable alerts; a forced rollback restores last-known-good image within the defined rollback window.
Automated test coverage: CI contains tests that fail if operator does not handle a proxy-auth failure, image-signature mismatch, or staged-mirror checksum drift.
Runbook validated: runbook covers recovery steps for at least 3 common failure scenarios (mirror unreachable, checksum mismatch, operator crash) and has been reviewed by SRE and security.
Security checks: acceptance requires signed image manifests validated with configured KMS and documented threat model updates completed by Security.
Backward compatibility: older client manifests (v1) still accepted with warnings and migration guidance surfaced in console/CLI.
Perf & SLO: in zero-egress mode, operator's upgrade window and health-check latency degradation are within the accepted SLOs listed in the PRD.
scope_notes: IN-SCOPE: profile schema (YAML/JSON) + server-side validation, operator state-machine changes for offline activation, telemetry gating controls, CI harness for offline scenarios, documentation and runbooks.
OUT-OF-SCOPE for this ticket: new network appliance implementations, UI redesign of the Console beyond minimal consent surfaces, licensing/pricing changes.
Assumptions: customers will provide at least one artifact mirror reachable during bootstrap unless explicitly using a sealed-image flow; HSM/KMS integrations exist per Private product baseline.
open_questions: Should profile declarations be editable post-bootstrap or immutable after initial activation? (tradeoff: flexibility vs reproducibility)
What is the precise rollback window we guarantee for offline/upgraded images before manual intervention is required?
Do we allow outbound DNS resolution in 'zero-egress' for validation (eg. CRL checks) if customers explicitly opt in?
How should operator telemetry toggles be surfaced in the API vs Console for programmatic automation?
Which existing KMS integrations are required to be supported at GA for secure manifest verification?
decisions: Adopt named profiles rather than freeform policy bundles to simplify onboarding and QA effort.
Operator will require an explicit 'artifact-accept' step for offline activation; no silent activation when signatures fail.
Telemetry in sealed / zero-egress mode will be opt-in and must be driven by a customer-provisioned, signed consent manifest.
Per-namespace egress exceptions will be implemented but require approver metadata and an audit trail stored locally and exportable.
CI test harness will simulate proxy failures and staged-mirror checksum drift as part of acceptance gating.
dependencies: SEC-102 (security: threat-model review and KMS approval)
